citations.locator: Vol. 1, § 38, The Jewish War and the Destruction of Jerusalem
citations.excerpt: It was burned on the tenth of August, a.d. 70, the same day of the year on which, according to tradition, the first temple was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar.

facts.value: Titus, son of the emperor Vespasian, conducted the Jewish war and destroyed Jerusalem and its temple.

citations.excerpt: His son, Titus, who himself ten years after became emperor

citations.locator: Vol. 1, § 38, The Jewish War and the Destruction of Jerusalem
citations.excerpt: then undertook the prosecution of the Jewish war, and became the instrument in the hand of God of destroying the holy city and the temple.

facts.value_before_verify: Roman forces under Titus destroyed Jerusalem and its temple.
